# System information

Memory, processor architecture and logical processor information.

<h2 id="memory-status-ex"><code>MemoryStatusEx</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct MemoryStatusEx {
    pub length: uint32;
    pub memoryLoad: uint32;
    pub totalPhysical: uint64;
    pub availablePhysical: uint64;
    pub totalPageFile: uint64;
    pub availablePageFile: uint64;
    pub totalVirtual: uint64;
    pub availableVirtual: uint64;
    pub availableExtendedVirtual: uint64;
}
```

The `MEMORYSTATUSEX` that [`GlobalMemoryStatusEx`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#global-memory-status-ex) fills in, with every size in bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L9)

**Fields**

| Name                       | Type     | Description                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `length`                   | `uint32` | The structure's size in bytes, `sizeof(MemoryStatusEx)`, which the caller sets before the call. |
| `memoryLoad`               | `uint32` | How much of the physical memory is in use, as a percentage from 0 to 100.                       |
| `totalPhysical`            | `uint64` | The physical memory the system can use.                                                         |
| `availablePhysical`        | `uint64` | The physical memory that is free or can be freed at once.                                       |
| `totalPageFile`            | `uint64` | The memory the system can commit, physical memory and page file together.                       |
| `availablePageFile`        | `uint64` | The part of that commit limit the calling process can still commit.                             |
| `totalVirtual`             | `uint64` | The user-mode address space of the calling process.                                             |
| `availableVirtual`         | `uint64` | The part of that address space neither reserved nor committed.                                  |
| `availableExtendedVirtual` | `uint64` | Reserved; always zero.                                                                          |

<h2 id="processor-relationship-header"><code>ProcessorRelationshipHeader</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct ProcessorRelationshipHeader {
    pub relationship: uint32;
    pub size: uint32;
}
```

The header that begins every record [`GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#get-logical-processor-information-ex) writes.
The records differ in size, so the buffer is walked by adding each record's `size` to reach the next one; the
rest of a record depends on its relationship and is not described here.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L34)

**Fields**

| Name           | Type     | Description                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relationship` | `uint32` | What the record describes, such as [`RelationProcessorCore`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#relation-processor-core). |
| `size`         | `uint32` | The record's size in bytes, header included.                                                                                |

<h2 id="global-memory-status-ex"><code>GlobalMemoryStatusEx</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GlobalMemoryStatusEx(status: *var MemoryStatusEx) -> bool32
```

Reports the machine's physical memory and how much of it, and of the commit limit, is in use.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-globalmemorystatusex](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-globalmemorystatusex)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L71)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type                  | Description                                                          |
| -------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status` | `*var MemoryStatusEx` | the structure to fill, with `length` set to `sizeof(MemoryStatusEx)` |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)

<h2 id="get-logical-processor-information-ex"><code>GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx(
    relationship: uint32,
    buffer: *var opaque,
    length: *var uint32
) -> bool32
```

Reads the processor relationships of one kind, such as one record per core, into a caller's buffer.
Asked with too small a buffer, or none, the call fails with [`ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER`](/docs/api/windows/errors#error-insufficient-buffer) and sets `length` to
the bytes needed, so it is called once to measure and once to fill.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getlogicalprocessorinformationex](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getlogicalprocessorinformationex)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L82)

**Parameters**

| Name           | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relationship` | `uint32`      | which records to write, such as [`RelationProcessorCore`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#relation-processor-core)                                             |
| `buffer`       | `*var opaque` | receives the records, each beginning with a [`ProcessorRelationshipHeader`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#processor-relationship-header), or null to measure |
| `length`       | `*var uint32` | how many bytes `buffer` holds on entry, and how many were written or are needed on return                                                                           |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)

<h2 id="get-native-system-info"><code>GetNativeSystemInfo</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetNativeSystemInfo(info: *var SystemInfo)
```

Reads what [`GetSystemInfo`](/docs/api/windows/system-info#get-system-info) does, but for the machine rather than for the calling process.
The two differ only under emulation, where an x86-64 program on an Arm machine is told it runs on x86-64 by
[`GetSystemInfo`](/docs/api/windows/system-info#get-system-info) and on Arm by this call. It cannot fail, and the structure is always filled.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getnativesysteminfo](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getnativesysteminfo)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L90)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type              | Description                     |
| ------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `info` | `*var SystemInfo` | receives the system information |

<h2 id="get-physically-installed-system-memory"><code>GetPhysicallyInstalledSystemMemory</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetPhysicallyInstalledSystemMemory(kilobytes: *var uint64) -> bool32
```

Reports the physical memory the firmware says is fitted, in kibibytes.
This is more than [`GlobalMemoryStatusEx`](/docs/api/windows/system-information#global-memory-status-ex) reports as total, by what the firmware and devices reserve. It fails
with `ERROR_INVALID_DATA` when the firmware's memory tables are missing or malformed.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getphysicallyinstalledsystemmemory](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getphysicallyinstalledsystemmemory)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/SystemInformation.rux#L99)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type          | Description                             |
| ----------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `kilobytes` | `*var uint64` | receives the fitted memory in kibibytes |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)
